mainTopic: When a doubtful קידושין or גירושין requires חליצה for the צרה, and when the Rabbis worried this would lead people to allow יבום.
overview: רבה and אביי continue arguing about why our משנה requires חליצה in a doubtful קידושין case but does not teach a doubtful גירושין case the same way. רבה says that in divorce, people might go from 'she does חליצה' to 'she may do יבום'. In the קידושין case that mistake would be harmless, because she stands on her חזקה. אביי challenges this from the collapsed-house case, where a doubt forbids a צרה despite her חזקה of being permitted. רבה answers in two ways. First, the Rabbis only made decrees for common cases like divorce. Second, in divorce people may think the Rabbis checked the גט, while nobody thinks a collapse can be solved. The גמרא then raises the משנה of a גט that lands halfway, where the צרה does חליצה with no worry. רבה and רב יוסף answer that that case has two contradicting sets of witnesses, which makes it a Torah-level doubt. The גמרא questions this and argues that two sets cancel out, bringing proof from בר שטיא's sale, and רב אשי's ruling there finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: Requiring חליצה shows it is only a stringency
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that because the משנה requires חליצה in the doubtful קידושין case, people will understand it is just a חומרא and will not draw wrong conclusions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since you require her to do חליצה, people will know that this is only an extra stringency.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing רבה's answer from just before. He says that requiring חליצה, rather than freeing her completely, sends a clear signal that the ruling is only strictness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that people might treat the doubtful קידושין as fully certain and make mistakes in related cases. רבה says the חליצה ruling itself prevents this. A full certain marriage would never be handled with just חליצה as a precaution, so people will see the ruling as a חומרא only.

keyTerms.meaning: the ceremony that frees a widow from her dead husband's brother

phrases.english: Since you require ḥalitza,
people will surely know that it is merely a stringency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבה's defense from the previous part of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Public perception: the form of the ruling shows that it is only a stringency.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: People might treat the doubtful קידושין as fully valid and make mistakes.
steps.terutzMaskana: Requiring חליצה signals that this is only a חומרא, so no mistake will follow.

steps.title: Then why not teach the divorce case with חליצה too?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges: if requiring חליצה shows it is just a stringency, the משנה could have taught a doubtful גירושין case the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the משנה should also teach the case of divorce, require חליצה there, and people would know it is only a stringency!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבה. If this trick works for קידושין, why didn't the משנה use it for a doubtful גירושין too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's reasoning seems to be a general tool: require חליצה, and everyone understands it is a חומרא. אביי argues that this tool should work just as well for a doubtful divorce. The fact that the משנה left out the divorce case suggests that רבה's explanation is missing something.

phrases.english: If so, let it teach divorce as well,
phrases.notes: This is אביי speaking. "It" means the משנה.

phrases.english: and require her to do ḥalitza,
and people would know that it is merely a stringency!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of step 1 by applying it to divorce.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that requiring חליצה signals a mere stringency.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the logic works, it should apply equally to the divorce case, yet the משנה does not teach that case.

steps.title: People would think she can also do יבום
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that in the divorce case people would reason that a woman who does חליצה may also do יבום, which would be a real problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say she does חליצה, people will say she may also do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains why the divorce case is different. Requiring חליצה there could lead people to wrongly allow יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People tend to assume that חליצה and יבום go together: any woman fit for one is fit for the other. In the divorce case, actually doing יבום would be forbidden. So a חליצה ruling there could lead people into a real sin.

phrases.english: If you say she does ḥalitza, then she will do yibum.
phrases.notes: He means people will mistakenly conclude this, not that it is really allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the divorce case has a further risk that the קידושין case seems not to have.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Divorce could be handled exactly like קידושין.
steps.terutzMaskana: In divorce, a חליצה ruling could lead people to allow a forbidden יבום.

steps.title: The same worry applies to the קידושין case
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the fear of people allowing יבום applies equally to the doubtful קידושין case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, if you say she does חליצה, people will say she may also do יבום!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי turns רבה's own answer back on him. The same mistake could happen in the קידושין case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's answer explained why the divorce case was left out. But the risk he names, that people will move from חליצה to יבום, is just as present in the קידושין case. So the difference between the two cases still needs to be explained.

phrases.english: Here too,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the doubtful קידושין case that רבה was defending.

phrases.english: if you say she does ḥalitza, then she will do yibum!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, אִם אַתָּה אוֹמֵר חוֹלֶצֶת, מִתְיַיבֶּמֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 3 by showing that its worry also applies to the original case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's distinction between divorce and קידושין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same mistaken reasoning, moving from חליצה to יבום, can happen in the קידושין case.

steps.title: Let her do יבום, since she stands on her חזקה
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that in the קידושין case it would not matter if she did יבום, because she stays on her original חזקה and no real sin is involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let her do יבום, and there is nothing wrong with that, because she stands on her presumed status.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה admits the mistake could happen in the קידושין case, but says it would be harmless there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The important difference is the חזקה. In the doubtful קידושין case, her starting status means that יבום would not actually break any prohibition. The חליצה is only a precaution. In the divorce case, by contrast, יבום would be a real sin.

keyTerms.meaning: there is nothing wrong with it
presumed status that stays in place until proven otherwise

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's principle is that when a woman's original חזקה permits her, a doubt only adds a stringency. If people err in a way that matches her חזקה, no real sin happens.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle, that a doubt does not override a permitting חזקה, is exactly what אביי attacks next.

phrases.english: So let her do yibum, and there is nothing wrong with that;
she stands on her presumed status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by admitting the mistake could happen but denying that it causes harm.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the premise and denies the harm.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A mistaken יבום in the קידושין case would be a real problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her חזקה makes יבום harmless in the קידושין case.

steps.title: אביי cites the collapsed house case
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a source: a house fell on a man and his wife, who was his niece, and no one knows who died first. Her צרה must do חליצה and may not do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: A house fell on a man and on his brother's daughter, and it is not known which of them died first. Her צרה does חליצה but does not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is setting up a new challenge by quoting a case. The actual question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband died first, his niece was still his wife at that moment. Her צרה is then exempt as the צרה of the יבם's daughter. If the niece died first, the צרה is a normal widow who needs יבום. Because of the doubt, the ruling is חליצה only, with no יבום.
steps.confusionAlert: The man was married to his niece. To the surviving brother, who is the יבם, she is his own daughter. That is why her צרה might be exempt from יבום.

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:

phrases.aramaic: נָפַל הַבַּיִת עָלָיו וְעַל בַּת אָחִיו,
phrases.english: A house fell on him and on his brother's daughter,
phrases.notes: His brother's daughter was also his wife.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין יָדוּעַ אֵיזֶה מֵהֶם מֵת רִאשׁוֹן,
phrases.english: and it is not known which of them died first;
her co-wife does ḥalitza but does not do yibum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that will be used to attack רבה's principle from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's principle that a doubt does not override a permitting חזקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step lays out the source. The contradiction is drawn in the next step.

steps.title: Why doesn't her חזקה keep her permitted?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: by רבה's logic, the צרה has a חזקה of being permitted to marry anyone, so a doubt should not forbid her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Here too, let us say: this woman has a חזקה of being permitted to marry anyone, and you come to forbid her because of a doubt. Do not forbid her because of a doubt!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now makes his challenge. If a חזקה wins over a doubt, why does the צרה need חליצה at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: All through her marriage, the צרה was exempt from יבום as the צרה of the יבם's daughter. So her חזקה was that she could marry anyone. Following רבה, a doubt should not take that away. Yet the source forbids her to others without חליצה, which seems to contradict רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: to the general public (to marry anyone)

phrases.english: Why? Here too, let us say:

phrases.aramaic: אִשָּׁה זוֹ בְּחֶזְקַת הֶיתֵּר לַשּׁוּק עוֹמֶדֶת,
phrases.english: This woman stands with a presumption of being permitted to the public,
phrases.notes: "The public" means she may marry any man, because she was always exempt from יבום.

phrases.english: and you come to forbid her because of a doubt;
do not forbid her because of a doubt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the source from step 6 against רבה's principle from step 5.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The צרה has a permitting חזקה, yet the source lets a doubt override it by requiring חליצה. This contradicts רבה's principle.

steps.title: Requiring חליצה in the collapse case should also lead to יבום
steps.stepSummary: אביי blocks a possible answer. Saying 'we are just being strict' does not help, because this strictness leads to a leniency: people will think a woman who does חליצה may also do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might say: here too, we are just being strict because of the doubt. But this is a stringency that leads to a leniency. If you say she does חליצה, people will think she may also do יבום!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is finishing his challenge from the house-collapse case. He blocks the answer 'we are only being strict here.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 3, רבה said that requiring חליצה in a doubtful divorce case could lead people to allow יבום. אביי says the same danger exists in the collapse case, where the צרה must do חליצה. So why are the Rabbis worried in one case and not the other?

keyTerms.meaning: A stringency that leads to a leniency
A co-wife (another wife of the same husband)

phrases.english: And if you would say: here too, we rule strictly
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the house-collapse case from step 6.

phrases.english: It is a stringency that leads to a leniency:
for if you say she does חליצה, she will come to do יבום!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's challenge by blocking the escape route of 'we are just being strict'.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim (step 3) that requiring חליצה leads people to allow יבום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same worry applies in the collapse case, yet there the צרה is still required to do חליצה.

steps.title: Divorce is common, collapses are rare
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the Rabbis only made decrees about common situations. Divorce is common; houses falling on people are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Divorce is common, so the Rabbis made a decree about it. House collapses are not common, so the Rabbis did not make a decree about them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains why the worry about יבום applies to divorce but not to the house collapse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Rabbis' decree is aimed at situations that happen often. A house falling on a couple is rare, so the Rabbis did not bother making a decree for it. That is why the צרה there may simply do חליצה.

phrases.english: Divorce, which is common —
the Rabbis made a decree about it;
collapses, which are not common —
the Rabbis did not make a decree about them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from the collapse case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the cases (common vs. rare)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worry about יבום should apply equally to divorce and to the collapse.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Rabbis only decreed for common cases like divorce, not rare ones like collapses.

steps.title: People think the Rabbis checked the גט, but nobody thinks they can solve a collapse
steps.stepSummary: A second answer. In divorce, people will think the Rabbis examined the גט and found it valid, so they will allow יבום. In a collapse, everyone knows the Rabbis cannot find out who died first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: in divorce, the ערוה is right there as a reminder. If you require her צרה to do חליצה, people will say: the Rabbis looked into the גט and found it is a proper גט. Then they will come to do יבום with the צרה. But a collapse? Could the Rabbis ever figure out anything about a collapse?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a different reason why the two cases are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a divorce, a גט can be checked. People may assume the Rabbis checked it, decided it was valid, and so the צרה is not a צרה of an ערוה, which would mean יבום is allowed. In a collapse, everyone knows nobody can tell who died first. So people understand the חליצה is only because of the doubt, and nobody will draw the wrong conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman forbidden as a close relative
They looked into it and established it

steps.confusionAlert: If the גט is valid, the divorced woman is no longer the husband's wife, so the other wife is not a 'צרה of an ערוה'. That is why people might wrongly think the צרה may do יבום.

phrases.english: Alternatively:
in divorce, where the ערוה is still there and serves as a sign,
phrases.notes: The divorced woman is alive and around, so people notice the case. The letter in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and you require her צרה to do חליצה,
people will say: the Rabbis looked into the גט
and found that it is a proper גט,
and they will come to do יבום with the צרה.

phrases.aramaic: מַפּוֹלֶת, מִי קָמוּ בְּהוּ רַבָּנַן בְּמַפּוֹלֶת?
phrases.english: A collapse — could the Rabbis ever figure out anything about a collapse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, separate answer to the same challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on how people will see the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Requiring חליצה looks the same in both cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only in divorce might people think the Rabbis decided the doubt in favor of a valid גט; in a collapse everyone knows the doubt can't be solved.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that rabbinic decrees can depend on what onlookers will mistakenly conclude, not only on the strict law.

steps.title: A משנה about a גט that lands halfway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה about a doubtful divorce: a גט thrown to a woman that lands exactly halfway between them. She is 'divorced and not divorced'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But regarding divorce, didn't we learn a משנה? We learned: if she was standing in a public area and he threw the גט to her, then if it landed closer to her, she is divorced. If it landed closer to him, she is not divorced. If it landed exactly halfway, she is divorced and not divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to רבה by quoting a משנה about a doubtful divorce. The punch comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a doubtful divorce, the very kind of case רבה said the Rabbis made a decree about. The גמרא will now show how that משנה treats the צרה.

phrases.english: And regarding divorce, didn't we learn?
But we learned:
If she was standing in a public area
and he threw it to her,
if it landed closer to her, she is divorced;
if closer to him, she is not divorced.
If exactly halfway,
she is divorced and not divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְגַבֵּי גֵירוּשִׁין מִי לָא תְּנַן? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a source that will challenge רבה's answers.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that in divorce cases the Rabbis decreed against requiring חליצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about a doubtful divorce is brought; its ruling will be shown in the next step.

steps.title: In the halfway-גט case the צרה does חליצה without worry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls the explanation of that משנה: the צרה of an ערוה must do חליצה. Nobody there says this will lead to יבום, which contradicts רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we asked: for what law does 'divorced and not divorced' matter? If he is a כהן, she is forbidden to him. If she is an ערוה, her צרה needs חליצה. And we do not say: if you say she does חליצה, she will come to do יבום!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא delivers the challenge. In a doubtful divorce, the צרה does חליצה, and nobody worries that this will lead to יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said that in divorce cases the Rabbis feared חליצה would lead to יבום. But this משנה is a doubtful divorce, and the צרה is told to do חליצה with no such concern. So רבה's distinction seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: A priest, who may not marry a divorcee

steps.whatToRemember: The halfway-גט משנה shows a doubtful divorce where the צרה does חליצה, with no fear that she will come to do יבום. This directly challenges רבה.

phrases.english: And we asked: for what law does this matter?
That if he is a כהן, she is forbidden to him;
and if she is an ערוה (to the brother-in-law),
her צרה needs חליצה.
And we do not say:
that if you say she does חליצה, she will come to do יבום!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 11 by drawing the conclusion from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's position that in doubtful divorce the Rabbis worried חליצה would lead to יבום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the halfway-גט case, a doubtful divorce, the צרה does חליצה and nobody raises the worry about יבום.

steps.title: Two sets of witnesses versus one set
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף explain that the thrown-גט משנה involves two contradicting sets of witnesses, which is a Torah-level doubt. Our משנה involves one set, which is only a rabbinic-level doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it already said about that משנה, by רבה and רב יוסף together, that it is about two sets of witnesses? One set says the גט landed closer to her, and the other says it landed closer to him. That is a Torah-level doubt. Our משנה is about one set of witnesses, so it is only a rabbinic-level doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 12 by showing that the two משניות are talking about different kinds of doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the thrown-גט case there are two full testimonies that contradict each other, so the doubt comes from the Torah, and the צרה must do חליצה no matter what. Our משנה has only one set of witnesses, so the doubt is only rabbinic. There the Rabbis could worry that חליצה would lead people to allow יבום. So the thrown-גט case does not contradict רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt about a Torah law, where we must be strict
A doubt that is only a rabbinic matter, where there is more room to be lenient
Closer to her (she is divorced) / closer to him (she is not divorced)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two משניות. Two sets of witnesses go with the thrown-גט משנה (a Torah-level doubt). One set goes with our משנה (a rabbinic-level doubt).

phrases.english: But wasn't it stated about it:
phrases.notes: "It" is the thrown-גט משנה from step 11.

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef, who both say:
Here we are dealing with two sets of witnesses,
one says: it landed closer to her,
and one says: it landed closer to him,
which makes it a Torah-level doubt.
But our משנה here is about one set of witnesses,
which makes it a rabbinic-level doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (אוקימתא): the two משניות deal with different kinds of doubt.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות are the same kind of doubt, so the thrown-גט case, which requires חליצה with no worry about יבום, contradicts רבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The thrown-גט case is a Torah-level doubt with two sets of witnesses, so חליצה is required there. Our משנה is a rabbinic-level doubt with one set, so the worry about יבום applies.

steps.title: How do we know our משנה is about one set of witnesses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the claim that our משנה deals with only one set of witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that our משנה is about one set of witnesses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof of the setup it just used in step 13. The next step will give the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 13 only works if our משנה really is about one set of witnesses. The משנה does not say this outright, so the גמרא wants a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: And from where do we know that our משנה here is about one set of witnesses?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the setup used in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that our משנה's divorce case involves only one set of witnesses.

steps.title: Divorce is like betrothal
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה puts doubtful divorce next to doubtful betrothal. Just as the betrothal case is one set of witnesses, so is the divorce case.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just like betrothal. Just as the betrothal case is about one set of witnesses, the divorce case is also about one set.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that our משנה lists doubtful קידושין and doubtful גירושין together, so both must be the same kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the two cases appear side by side, they are read the same way. This moves the question to the קידושין case. If that one is about one set of witnesses, the divorce case is too.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, read the same way as

phrases.english: It is like betrothal:
just as betrothal is with one set of witnesses,
so too divorce is with one set of witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The divorce case is read the same way as the neighboring betrothal case, which involves one set of witnesses.

steps.title: How do we know the betrothal case is one set?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the betrothal case itself involves one set of witnesses. Maybe it involves two sets.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the betrothal case itself, how do we know it is about one set of witnesses? Maybe it is about two sets?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes one step further back and asks for proof about the קידושין case. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 rested completely on the קידושין case being one set of witnesses. If that case could be two sets, the comparison proves nothing.

phrases.english: And betrothal itself,
from where do we know it is with one set of witnesses?
Perhaps it is with two sets of witnesses?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the basis of the answer in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that the betrothal case in our משנה involves only one set of witnesses.

steps.title: With two sets, she could simply do יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if the betrothal case were two sets of witnesses, the צרה could do יבום with no problem. Since the משנה does not allow that, it must be one set.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were two sets of witnesses, she could do יבום, and there would be nothing wrong with that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove that the קידושין case must be one set of witnesses, because two sets would lead to a different ruling than the one in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that with two sets, there are witnesses saying the betrothal never took effect. Then her co-wife would not be a צרת ערוה and could do יבום. The משנה does not rule that way, so the case must be one set.

keyTerms.meaning: Let her do יבום (marry her late husband's brother)
There is nothing wrong with that

phrases.english: If it were with two sets of witnesses,
let her do יבום, and there is nothing wrong with that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two sets would allow יבום, and the משנה does not allow it, so the case must be one set.

steps.title: But witnesses say it landed close to her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects step 17. There are witnesses saying the betrothal object landed close to her, so how can we allow יבום with no problem?
steps.simpleTranslation: There are witnesses standing here saying it landed closer to her, and you say she can do יבום with nothing wrong?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer in step 17 and says it makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two sets, one set says the object landed close to her, which means she was betrothed. Then her co-wife is a צרת ערוה and may not do יבום. We cannot just ignore those witnesses and allow יבום.

phrases.english: Witnesses are standing and saying it landed closer to her,
and you say let her do יבום
and there is nothing wrong with that?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 17 that two sets of witnesses in the betrothal case would allow יבום with no problem.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One of the two sets testifies that she was betrothed. That testimony cannot be ignored, so allowing יבום is not obviously fine.

steps.title: Two sets of witnesses is also only a rabbinic-level doubt
steps.stepSummary: A second attack: even two contradicting sets of witnesses create only a rabbinic-level doubt. The two testimonies cancel out, and the woman stays in her original status.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, even with two sets of witnesses it is only a rabbinic-level doubt. We say: put the two witnesses against the other two, and leave the woman in her original status!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the main distinction of רבה and רב יוסף from step 13, which said that two sets of witnesses make a Torah-level doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two pairs of witnesses contradict each other, the testimonies cancel out and we go back to the woman's previous status (חזקה). By Torah law that settles it, so any remaining doubt is only rabbinic. This erases the difference between the two משניות.

keyTerms.meaning: Put two witnesses against two: the testimonies cancel each other out
Presumed status: what we assume because that is how things were before

steps.whyThisMatters: If this challenge stands, the answer of רבה and רב יוסף in step 13 falls apart, and the contradiction from step 12 comes back.

phrases.english: And furthermore, with two sets of witnesses too,
it is a rabbinic-level doubt,
for we say: place two witnesses against two,
and place the woman on her presumed status!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ — בִּשְׁתֵּי כִּיתֵּי עֵדִים נָמֵי, סְפֵיקָא דְרַבָּנַן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, deeper challenge after step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction of רבה and רב יוסף (step 13) that two sets of witnesses create a Torah-level doubt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradicting testimonies cancel out and the woman keeps her original status, so by Torah law there is no doubt. Any doubt left is only rabbinic, just like the one-set case.

steps.title: Proof from the case of בר שטיא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports step 19 with the case of בר שטיא, who sold property. One pair of witnesses said he was sane at the time and another pair said he was insane, and רב אשי ruled that the two pairs cancel out.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just like the case of בר שטיא's property. בר שטיא sold property. Two witnesses came and said he sold it while healthy, and two others came and said he sold it while insane. רב אשי said: put the two against the two...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real case to prove that two contradicting pairs of witnesses cancel out. רב אשי's ruling finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר שטיא was sometimes sane and sometimes not, so the witnesses disagreed about whether his sale was valid. רב אשי's ruling, 'two against two', shows that contradicting testimonies are treated as canceling each other out, which is exactly the claim of step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who sometimes went insane (literally 'son of a fool')

phrases.english: Just like the case of the property of Bar Shatya.
For Bar Shatya sold property.
Two witnesses came and said:
he sold it when he was healthy,
and two others came and said:
he sold it when he was insane.
And Rav Ashi said:
place two witnesses against two,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings proof for the claim of step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that two contradicting sets of witnesses cancel out, so the doubt is only rabbinic.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אשי's ruling in the case of בר שטיא's property sale.
